keyVerseText: All these were of costly stones, according to the measures of hewed stones, sawed with saws, within and without, even from the foundation unto the coping, and so on the outside toward the great court.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun מַסַּד (maççad) derives from the root יָסַד (yâçad), which carries the fundamental idea of setting or establishing something firmly. This root emphasizes the act of founding or laying a base with intentionality and strength, beyond the simple notion of a physical foundation. The etymology highlights the concept of something deliberately appointed or fixed in place to provide stability and support.
usageInScripture: The word מַסַּד appears with a consistent meaning related to a physical foundation, as seen in its single recorded occurrence in 1 Kings 7:9. The phrase 'even from the foundation' underscores the thoroughness and precision of the construction described, indicating that the foundation is a critical starting point. This usage reveals that מַסַּד is closely tied to the idea of a foundational element upon which something greater is built, both literally and figuratively.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מַסַּד as a foundation rooted in the concept of deliberate establishment enriches our grasp of biblical teaching about stability and security in God. Foundations are essential for enduring structures, symbolizing the reliability and permanence of God's covenant and promises. For the Christian faith, this word points us to Christ as the ultimate foundation upon which the church is built, established firmly by God’s sovereign will and purpose. Recognizing the intentionality behind the foundation encourages believers to trust in God’s unshakable work in their lives and in salvation history.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Kings 7:9, the description of the stones being hewed and sawed 'even from the foundation unto the coping' emphasizes the meticulous care in the temple's construction. The use of מַסַּד here highlights that the strength and beauty of the structure begin at its very base. This reminds us that true strength and glory in God's dwelling come from a solid, well-laid foundation, symbolizing God’s enduring presence and faithfulness from the very beginning.
